claims.statement: SWE-bench benchmark evaluations show that unassisted state-of-the-art foundation models resolve under 5 percent of real-world software engineering tasks without structured execution feedback and tool sandboxes.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Across 2,294 real-world GitHub issues from 12 popular Python repositories, Claude 2 solved 4.8% and GPT-4 solved 1.7%, demonstrating that state-of-the-art models fail on over 95% of issues without sandboxed execution feedback.
limitations: Based on the SWE-bench evaluation benchmark of 2,294 GitHub issues across 12 open-source Python repositories
script_spans: Empirical benchmarks on real-world repositories show frontier models fail on over ninety-five percent of software tasks without structured execution sandboxes.

claims.statement: Unconstrained multi-turn agent execution without formal tool boundaries and schemas leads to compounding hallucination cascades and state divergence.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Empirical evaluations in MetaGPT demonstrate that unstructured multi-agent discussions frequently collapse into circular loops and hallucination cascades, whereas structured Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) achieve robust task execution.
limitations: Measured on multi-agent software engineering benchmarks with complex dependency graphs
script_spans: When agents execute raw bash commands without boundaries, unconstrained multi-step runs easily diverge or corrupt local workspace state.

claims.statement: Deterministic shadow simulation (dry-run) eliminates live state mutations while verifying permission envelopes end-to-end.

source.publisher: Google Cloud DORA (DevOps Research and Assessment)

claims.evidence_excerpt: Automated dry-runs, continuous testing, and verified rollback boundaries prevent destructive production outages and eliminate unauthorized state mutations.
limitations: Requires mock transport coverage for all outbound publisher endpoints
script_spans: Shadow dry-runs prove zero mutations and zero unverified uploads before any byte reaches production.
